epithet: The Prophet’s household, and four women
lede: A private matter between the Prophet ﷺ and his wives was made part of the Qurʾan — not to embarrass anyone, but because his household is the pattern for every other. The surah ends with four women whose stories prove that no one is saved, or lost, by whom they are married to.

names.name: al-Taḥrīm
names.note: From its first ayah: “Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?” It is also called by its opening, Lima tuḥarrim, and al-Qurṭubī records the name Sūrat al-Nabī, the Surah of the Prophet.

revelation.detail: It is Madinan in the saying of all. It belongs to the later years in Madinah, when the Prophet’s ﷺ household had grown to several wives; ʿUmar’s long account of the affair, in the two Ṣaḥīḥs, mentions the fear at the time of an attack by the Ghassānids, which places it near the ninth year.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ التَّحْرِيمِ وَهِيَ مَدَنِيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
سُورَةُ التَّحْرِيمِ مَدَنِيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ، وَهِيَ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ آيَةً. وَتُسَمَّى سُورَةَ "النَّبِيِّ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، والبَيْهَقِيُّ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ «التَّحْرِيمِ» بِالمَدِينَةِ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Madinah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: Two accounts are given of what the Prophet ﷺ had forbidden himself. In the one narrated by ʿĀʾishah in both Ṣaḥīḥs, he used to stay a while with his wife Zaynab bint Jaḥsh and drink honey there. ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah agreed that whichever of them he came to next would say that she noticed on him the smell of maghāfīr, a strong-scented gum. He said: “No — I drank honey at Zaynab’s, and I will not do so again; I have sworn it. Tell no one.” In the other, reported by Anas, he had sworn off his bondwoman Māriyah to satisfy his wives. Ibn Kathīr mentions both, and the scholars note that the two may both be true.

Either way the correction is the same. A prophet’s choices become his community’s law. He cannot, to please the people around him, treat as forbidden what Allah has permitted; and the way out of an oath of that kind has already been ordained.

Then the surah speaks to the two wives directly — “if you both turn to Allah in repentance, for your hearts have inclined” — and it does so with a force that astonished Ibn ʿAbbās, who waited a year for the courage to ask ʿUmar who the two were. ʿUmar told him: ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah — his own daughter.

From the Prophet’s ﷺ house the surah turns to everyone’s: “O you who believe, guard yourselves and your families against a Fire.” And it closes with four women. The wives of Nūḥ and of Lūṭ lived under the roofs of two prophets and were lost. The wife of Pharaoh lived under the roof of the worst of tyrants and asked her Lord for a house near Him in the Garden. And Maryam had no husband at all.

occasions.title: The honey
occasions.text: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to drink honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jaḥsh and stay with her. Ḥafṣah and I agreed that whichever of us he came to would say: have you eaten maghāfīr? I find the smell of maghāfīr on you. He said: ‘No, but I was drinking honey at Zaynab bint Jaḥsh’s, and I will not return to it; I have sworn. Do not tell anyone.’”

occasions.title: Māriyah
occasions.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had a bondwoman with whom he was intimate, and ʿĀʾishah and Ḥafṣah kept at him until he made her forbidden to himself. So Allah sent down: “O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?”
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: al-Nasāʾī (3959); its chain is ṣaḥīḥ according to al-Albānī.

evidence.quote: اختلُف فِي سَبَبِ نُزُولِ صَدْرِ هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ، فَقِيلَ: نَزَلَتْ فِي شَأْنِ مَارِيَةَ، وَكَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَدْ حَرَّمَهَا

occasions.title: The two who backed each other
occasions.text: Ibn ʿAbbās said: for a year I wanted to ask ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb about an ayah, and could not, out of awe of him — until he went out on the Pilgrimage and I went with him. On the way back he turned aside into the thorn trees for a need of his; I waited for him, then walked on with him, and said: “Commander of the Faithful, who were the two among the wives of the Prophet ﷺ who backed each other against him?” He said: “Those were Ḥafṣah and ʿĀʾishah.”
story: ʿUmar told him to ask about whatever he thought he had knowledge of, and went on: “By Allah, in the days of ignorance we counted women as nothing, until Allah sent down about them what He sent down, and apportioned to them what He apportioned. One day I was turning a matter over, and my wife said: If only you did such-and-such. I said: What is it to you? She said: How strange you are, Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb! You will not be answered back — and your own daughter answers back the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he spends his day angry.”

He took up his cloak and went straight to Ḥafṣah. “Daughter, do you answer back the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he spends his day angry?” She said: “By Allah, we do answer him back.” He said: “Know that I am warning you of the punishment of Allah and the anger of His Messenger. Daughter, do not be misled by the one whose beauty has made her bold, and the love the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has for her” — he meant ʿĀʾishah. Then he went in to Umm Salamah, who was his kinswoman, and spoke to her; and she said: “How strange you are, Ibn al-Khaṭṭāb! You have entered into everything, until now you want to come between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his wives.” “By Allah,” he said, “she took me up in a way that broke some of what I was feeling.”

He had a friend among the Helpers; when one of them was away, the other brought him the news. They were in fear at that time of one of the kings of Ghassān, who was said to be making ready to march on them. One night the friend beat at the door: “Open, open!” — “Has the Ghassānī come?” — “Worse than that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has withdrawn from his wives.”

He found the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in an upper room reached by a ladder, a servant of his at the head of the steps, and was given leave to enter. He told him the whole of this, and when he reached what Umm Salamah had said, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. He was lying on a mat with nothing between him and it, under his head a leather cushion stuffed with palm fibre; at his feet a heap of tanning leaves, and by his head some hides hung up. “I saw the mark of the mat on his side, and I wept. He said: ‘What makes you weep?’ I said: Messenger of Allah, Chosroes and Caesar live as they live — and you are the Messenger of Allah. He said: ‘Are you not content that this world should be theirs, and the Hereafter ours?’”
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās, from ʿUmar: al-Bukhārī (4913) and Muslim (1479).

aim: The upbringing of the Prophet’s ﷺ household, that it may be the model for the family and for society.
themes: Guarding one’s family from the Fire

outline.title: To the Prophet ﷺ and his wives
outline.summary: O Prophet, why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking to please your wives? Allah has ordained for you the release from your oaths. The Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives; when she disclosed it and Allah made it known to him, he told her part and passed over part. If you two turn to Allah in repentance — your hearts have inclined. But if you support each other against him, Allah is his Protector, and Jibrīl, and the righteous among the believers, and the angels besides.

outline.title: To every household
outline.summary: O you who believe, guard yourselves and your families against a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels stern and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands. O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance (66:8): it may be that your Lord will remove your misdeeds from you and admit you to gardens, on the Day He will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him, their light running before them.

outline.title: To the Prophet ﷺ again
outline.summary: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be firm with them. Their refuge is Hell.

outline.title: Four women
outline.summary: Allah sets forth an example for the disbelievers: the wife of Nūḥ and the wife of Lūṭ. They were under two of Our righteous servants and betrayed them, and those two availed them nothing against Allah. And an example for the believers: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, “My Lord, build for me a house near You in the Garden, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds”; and Maryam daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, and affirmed the words of her Lord and His Books, and was of the devout.

keyAyah.why: The surah’s lesson, widened from one house to all: a believer is answerable for those under his roof.

virtues.text: “Many among men have reached perfection, but among women none reached it except Āsiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and Maryam, the daughter of ʿImrān. And the excellence of ʿĀʾishah over other women is as the excellence of tharīd over other food.”

before: Al-Ṭalāq legislated for the ending of a marriage. Al-Taḥrīm shows a household kept together — by correction, repentance and an oath undone.
after: Al-Taḥrīm ends with four people each judged on their own deeds. Al-Mulk opens with the reason: He created death and life to test which of you is best in deed.
